mappings.note: A system blending theocratic and democratic elements under a Supreme Leader. Comparative government under the goal.
Power seized by force, no constitution, opposition suppressed - dictatorship identified. Comparative government.
The executive drawn from and answerable to the legislature in a parliamentary system. The working of Indian democracy's institutions.
Matches dictators to the countries they ruled. Used in the chapter to illustrate dictatorship, so the comparative-government goal.
Statements about dictatorship, keyed on the suppression of fundamental rights. A contrast with democratic government, so the goal.
The judicial function of interpreting law and settling disputes. An organ of government under the goal.
Authority from the people against authority from religion. Comparative government under the goal.

The Chandrapida story turns on a king delivering justice even to the humblest subject, which is the chapter's illustration of equal treatment under the law. Not the bare goal, because the point being tested is equality before justice.
Why an independent judiciary matters to a healthy democracy. An institution of democracy under the goal.
Laws from sacred texts and a divinely sanctioned head of state identified as theocracy. Comparative government.
Finds the wrong country-to-government pairing. Comparative government under the goal.
Completes 'separation of powers' for the three organs. A constitutional principle under the goal.
Life under surveillance with rules on dress and internet access identified as dictatorship. Comparative government, shown through a lived example.
Free elections, accountability and protected rights resolved to democracy. A whole-system identification under the goal.
Rejects the wrong country-and-government-type example. Comparative government.

Accepts that democracies face corruption and wealth disparity but rejects the claim that democracy exists to serve an elite. A judgement about how democracy works, so the goal rather than the economic-equality outcome.
The directly elected Lower House against the Upper House. Legislative structure, so the goal; LO-179 is reserved for items about the electoral process itself.
Inherited, unconstrained power identified as absolute monarchy. Comparative government.

A few wealthy interests dominating policy read as a drift towards oligarchy. A judgement about a form of government, so the goal; LO-176 would fit an item that sorted economic from political equality as concepts.
Sorts the real reasons democracy is valued - equal rights, freedom, accountability - from a false one. The value of equality carries the item, so LO-175.

Names the Holocaust, the chapter's extreme illustration of what unchecked dictatorial power did to a people's rights. Kept in the civics lane because the chapter uses it as the counter-case to constitutional protection of rights.
Defines 'adjudicating' as settling legal disputes. Vocabulary of the judicial organ, so the goal.
Accepts the Uttaramerur evidence for elected local bodies and rejects the claim that they were powerless. Local democratic process, which the goal explicitly covers.
Rejects the claim that fundamental rights are optional guidelines. Constitutional values under the goal.
Completes 'presidential' for a system with a separately elected executive. Comparative government.
Defines a representative in democratic governance. The working of representative democracy, so the goal.

Dating women's federal suffrage in Switzerland to the 20th century is about how recently equal voting rights were won. The significance of equality in democracy, so LO-175 rather than the general goal.
Different democratic forms read as adaptations to different countries. Comparative government under the goal.
The judiciary holding both citizens and government to the law. An institution of democracy, so the goal.
Bhishma's counsel in the Shanti Parva on good governance and a ruler's moral duty. The chapter uses it for standards of rule, so the civics goal.
What universal adult franchise guarantees - an equal vote for every adult citizen. Political equality, so LO-175, in line with the other franchise item.

Names the Arthashastra as Kautilya's treatise. A text-and-author recall, which belongs to the history goal's sources clause; the item elsewhere that asks what Kautilya said government is for was given CG-SST3 because it is about the purpose of government.
Two houses signifying a bicameral legislature. Legislative structure under the goal.
Compares the unlimited power of an absolute monarch with the limited role of a constitutional one. Comparative government.
Defines fundamental rights in a democracy. Constitutional values, which the goal names; LO-175 is kept for items where equality specifically is the point.
A body testing laws against the constitution and settling disputes about them is performing the judicial function. An organ of government under the goal.
Sorts the features of a dictatorship from a non-feature. Comparative government under the goal.
'Rajadharma' as the duty and righteous conduct expected of a king. Used in this chapter as an early standard for accountable rule, so the civics goal.

A caricature defined through the drawings of Hitler and Idi Amin - political cartooning, which is how media comments on power. LO-182 is the frame's only media outcome; the item is a narrow one, but no other legal code touches media at all.
